name: bkfe
title: Compute a Binned Kernel Functional Estimate

origin.description: Returns an estimate of a binned approximation to the kernel estimate of the specified density functional. The kernel is the standard normal density.
origin.usage:
bkfe(x, drv, bandwidth, gridsize = 401L, range.x,
     binned = FALSE, truncate = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector of observations. Missing values are not allowed.

arguments.name: drv
arguments.text: Order of derivative in the density functional. Must be a non-negative even integer.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced points over which binning is performed.

arguments.name: range.x
arguments.text: Minimum and maximum values of x at which to compute the estimate. When binned is FALSE, the default is the minimum and maximum data values. When binned is TRUE, range.x must be supplied.

arguments.name: binned
arguments.text: If TRUE, x is taken to be grid counts rather than raw data.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If TRUE, data outside range.x are ignored.

origin.details: The density functional of order drv is the integral of the product of the density and its drv-th derivative. Kernel estimates of such quantities use a binned implementation and the standard normal kernel.
origin.value: The estimated functional, a single number.

translation.description: Returns an estimate of a binned approximation to the kernel estimate of the specified density functional. The kernel is the standard normal density.
translation.usage:
bkfe(x, drv, bandwidth, gridsize=401, range_x=None,
     binned=False, truncate=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric sample, or grid counts when binned is true. Missing values are not allowed.

arguments.name: drv
arguments.text: Order of derivative in the density functional. Must be a non-negative even integer.

arguments.name: bandwidth
arguments.text: Kernel bandwidth. Must be supplied and strictly positive.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced points over which binning is performed. Ignored when binned is true; the length of x is the grid then.

arguments.name: range_x
arguments.text: The two endpoints at which to compute the estimate. This is range.x in R. When binned is false, None uses the minimum and maximum data values. When binned is true, range_x is required.

arguments.name: binned
arguments.text: If true, x is taken to be grid counts rather than raw data.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If true, observations outside range_x are ignored. Used only when binned is false.

translation.details: The density functional of order drv is the integral of the product of the density and its drv-th derivative. Bin counts, when the data are not already binned, come from the Rust crate linbin. The normal-kernel weights and the FFT stay in NumPy.
translation.value: The estimated functional, a single number.
translation.example:
from mass import geyser
from kernsmooth import bkfe

x = geyser["duration"]
est = bkfe(x, drv=4, bandwidth=0.3)
